entities.summary: Teppe Hasanlu or Hasanlitepe, also known as just Hasanlu, is an archeological site of an ancient city located in the West Azerbaijan province of Iran, a short distance south of Lake Urmia. The nature of its destruction at the end of the 9th century BC essentially froze one layer of the city in time, providing researchers with extremely well preserved buildings, artifacts, and skeletal remains from the victims and enemy combatants of the attack. The site was likely associated with the Mannaeans and possibly with the Armenians. Teppe Hasanlu is a archaeological site from Asia. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Teppe Hasanlu's well-preserved buildings and artifacts provide valuable insights into the Mannaeans' culture and their interactions with neighboring civilizations. The site's unique preservation of skeletal remains from the victims of a 9th century BC attack offers a rare glimpse into the lives of ancient combatants.
